{{Short description|American chemist}}
'''Alan S. Goldman''' is an [[Americans|American]] [[chemist]] and [[Distinguished Professor]] of [[Chemistry]] at [[Rutgers University-New Brunswick]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Goldman, Alan |url=https://chem.rutgers.edu/research/faculty-research/149-goldman-alan |website=chem.rutgers.edu |accessdate=21 November 2018 |language=en-gb}}</ref>  Goldman's research area is [[homogeneous catalysis]] with emphasis on [[C-H activation]] and functionalization of hydrocarbons,<ref>{{cite journal |doi=10.1021/cr1003503 |title=Dehydrogenation and Related Reactions Catalyzed by Iridium Pincer Complexes |date=2011 |last1=Choi |first1=Jongwook |last2=MacArthur |first2=Amy H. Roy |last3=Brookhart |first3=Maurice |last4=Goldman |first4=Alan S. |journal=Chemical Reviews |volume=111 |issue=3 |pages=1761–1779 |pmid=21391566 }}</ref> and the reduction of dinitrogen.<ref>{{cite journal |doi=10.1021/acscatal.0c02606 |title=Considering Electrocatalytic Ammonia Synthesis via Bimetallic Dinitrogen Cleavage |date=2020 |last1=Bruch |first1=Quinton J. |last2=Connor |first2=Gannon P. |last3=McMillion |first3=Noah D. |last4=Goldman |first4=Alan S. |last5=Hasanayn |first5=Faraj |last6=Holland |first6=Patrick L.|last7=Miller |first7=Alexander J. M.|journal=ACS Catalysis |volume=10 |pages=10826–10846|doi-access=free }}</ref>
[[File:GoldmanPincer.svg|thumb|Iridium pincer complex for alkane dehydrogenation.<ref>{{cite journal |doi=10.1021/jacs.1c13309 |title=Reactivity of Iridium Complexes of a Triphosphorus-Pincer Ligand Based on a Secondary Phosphine. Catalytic Alkane Dehydrogenation and the Origin of Extremely High Activity |date=2022 |last1=Gordon |first1=Benjamin M. |last2=Lease |first2=Nicholas |last3=Emge |first3=Thomas J. |last4=Hasanayn |first4=Faraj |last5=Goldman |first5=Alan S. |journal=Journal of the American Chemical Society |volume=144 |issue=9 |pages=4133–4146 |pmid=35224972 |bibcode=2022JAChS.144.4133G |osti=1866620 |url=https://www.osti.gov/biblio/1866620 }}</ref>]]

==Recognition==
Goldman has been recognized by numerous awards. He was awarded the ACS [[Catalysis]] Lectureship for the Advancement of Catalytic Science in 2018.<ref>{{cite web |title=Professor Alan Goldman Interview |url=https://pubs.acs.org/page/accacs/goldman/interview.html |website=pubs.acs.org |accessdate=21 November 2018 |language=en}}</ref>  He received the ACS Award in [[Organometallic chemistry|Organometallic Chemistry]] in 2019<ref>{{cite web |last1=Meerovich |first1=Amy |title=Congratulations Alan Goldman! |url=https://chem.rutgers.edu/news-events/2018-news/1288-alan-goldman-recipient-of-the-2019-acs-award-in-organometallic-chemistry |website=chem.rutgers.edu |accessdate=21 November 2018 |language=en-gb}}</ref> and the Sir Geoffrey Wilkinson Award from the Royal Society of Chemistry (UK) in 2020.<ref>{{cite web |title=Royal Society of Chemistry 2020 prize and award winners |url=https://www.rsc.org/awards-funding/awards/2020-winners/ |website=rsc.org |accessdate=5 September 2020 |language=en}}</ref> In 2021, he was elected as a Fellow of the American Association for the Advancement of Science.<ref>{{cite web |title=2021 AAAS Fellows |url=https://www.aaas.org/page/2021-fellows |website=aaas.org |accessdate=24 May 2022 |language=en-gb}}</ref>
